column2: GT Independence — Engineering Coding Standards Checklist

column6: Signals in a service for reactive state management
column8: Client is on Angular 13; Signals are unavailable until framework upgrade.
column9: Implement NgRx Store or RxJS Subject-in-a-Service pattern

column6: Centralized enterprise state management via NgRx
column8: Highly recommended for enterprise scale; robust despite initial boilerplate.
Built-in template control flow cannot compile in Angular 13.

column6: Mandatory trackBy functions on all *ngFor loops
column8: Prevents DOM thrashing and guarantees optimal collection rendering performance.

column6: Component initialization / data-fetching calls in Ionic lifecycle hooks i.e ionViewWillEnter, ionViewDidEnter instead of the constructor or Angular lifecycle hooks.
column8: Execute data fetching in ionViewWillEnter/ionViewDidEnter to handle view navigation and cached Ionic page re-entry.
column9: Use ngOnInit only for one-time setup that does not need refresh on page re-entry

column6: Keep components focused on presentation and interaction. Put API access, business rules, and native integrations in services.
column8: Enforce separation of concerns by delegating business logic, native integrations, and HTTP requests to injectable services.
column9: Injectable services (@Injectable) for API and logic; thin presentational components

column6: Avoid nested subscriptions. Choose operators intentionally: switchMap for replacing stale requests
column8: Eliminate nested .subscribe() blocks by flattening streams using RxJS higher-order mapping operators.
column9: Higher-order mapping: switchMap (cancel stale), concatMap (sequential), mergeMap (concurrent)

column6: Strict subscription teardown on component destroy
column8: takeUntilDestroyed() is Angular 16+; enforce takeUntil pattern in ngOnDestroy.
column9: Prefer async pipe binding in templates whenever possible

column8: Enforce modular selector nesting (max depth 3) to prevent specificity bloat and CSS bleeding.

column6: Standardize indentation via .prettierrc (2 spaces, useTabs: false, tabWidth: 2)
column8: Configure root .prettierrc and .editorconfig to maintain uniform formatting across teams.
column9: Enforce via EditorConfig and pre-commit hook (lint-staged)

column6: Extend a shared Angular component or Ionic page base class to provide stubs for commonly used methods (e.g., export class MyPage extends GTIPage)
column8: Use abstract base classes (e.g., GTIPage) to standardize boilerplate methods, navigation helpers, and common lifecycle hooks.

column6: Use take(1) only when the requirement is to consume one emission. If no emission occurs, the subscription remains active unless another cleanup mechanism ends it.
column8: Do not rely solely on take(1) for teardown if the source may never emit; combine with takeUntil or component teardown.
column9: Pair with takeUntil(destroy$) or prefer async pipe
